newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FIGURE SKATING-OLYMPIC CHAMPION WINS BAILEY'S CUP.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-OLYMPIC CHAMPION WINS BAILEY'S CUP.

text.p: Olympic champion Alexei Urmanov swept majestically to victory in front of his home crowd in the men's competition at the Bailey's Cup of Russia Champions Series figure skating event on Saturday.
Leading after the short programme, Urmanov skated last in the free skating and performed a programme packed with technical difficulty.
He successfully landed two triple jump combinations, opening his programme with a triple axel-triple toe loop and then following with a triple flip-triple toe loop and three more triples.
There were minor wobbles on two landings but his marks included three 5.8s for technical merit followed by one 6.0 and six 5.9s for presentation.
This second win in the Champions Series gives Urmanov a maximum 24 points in the Series and he heads the qualifiers for the final in Hamilton, Canada in February.
"This wasn't the World Championships but it was a hard competition," said Urmanov afterwards. "Men's skating is at such a high level now that I don't envy the judges their job."

Training partner Alexei Yagudin finished second to score nine Champions Series points and secure a place in the final. Yagudin also landed a triple axel-triple toe loop combination and five more triples, earning one 5.9 and seven 5.8s.

"I knew Yagudin skated well," said Urmanov. "I saw his marks but not his performance and he could have beaten me as he did here last time." That defeat was in the Centennial in Ice competition last February.
American Michael Weiss failed on his attempted quadruple toe loop but landed five triples to hold onto third place. He has not qualified for the final.
The men's field in Hamilton will comprise Urmanov, Yagudin, Canada's Elvis Stojko, Ilya Kulik of Russia and Dmitry Dmitrenko from Ukraine.

The sixth place will be decided on Monday when the ISU Champions Series Management Committee meet to ratify the Series results and make a decision about world champion Todd Eldredge after the American withdrew injured from his second scoring event in Japan last weekend.
In the ice dance competition Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov of Russia took the title after leading the competition throughout.

In the free dance section the judges awarded them one score of 6.0 and six 5.9s for their fast-paced, dramatic waltz. It was a non-scoring event in the Champions Series for the world sliver medallists, who have already qualified for the final.
European champion Irina Slutskaya made it three wins for Russia as she moved up from third place after the short programme to win the free skating and take the women's title.

Slutskaya had already qualified for the final with maximum points from her two points scoring competitions. She could only land three triples cleanly, but her overall performance was enough to win her a 6-1 majority verdict from the judges.
